item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - WINTER STORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Winter Weather Warning | Yellow Warning - Winter Storm - In Effect |

Hazardous winter conditions are expected due to: - Snow - Blowing snow - Wind A significant, long duration snowfall event is expected to bring total snowfall accumulations of 30 to 50 cm by Sunday morning. Precipitation will begin as rain late Friday afternoon before transitioning to heavy snow Friday evening. Heavy snow will continue through Friday night and through Saturday before gradually tapering off on Sunday. In addition to the snowfall, strong northerly winds with gusts up to 70 km/h will develop Friday night and persist through Saturday into Sunday. These winds, combined with falling snow, will result in significantly reduced visibility at times in snow and blowing snow. Winds will gradually ease through the day Sunday. Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced to near-zero at times. Local utility outages are likely. Property or tree damage is possible. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using SKStorm.

| Moderate - possible threat | Expected - act within an hour

item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - WINTER STORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Winter Weather Warning | Yellow Warning - Winter Storm - In Effect |

Hazardous winter conditions are expected due to: - Snow - Freezing rain - Wind - Rain A significant fall storm will impact northern Manitoba beginning Friday evening and will persist through the weekend. Where: Areas of northern Manitoba, including, Pukatawagan, Lynn Lake, Brochet, and Tadoule Lake. What: Hazardous winter conditions including: Heavy snow with total amounts of 20 to 40 cm. Severe wind gusts possibly exceeding 90 km/h. Significantly reduced visibilities in blowing snow Freezing rain Heavy rain with total amounts of 20 to 40 mm. When: Precipitation and strong northerly winds will move into northern Manitoba overnight Friday into Saturday morning and begin mostly as rain or freezing rain. This will transition to snow throughout the day on Saturday before tapering off Sunday afternoon. Winds will strengthen throughout the day on Saturday with gusts up to 90 km/h in areas closer to the Nunavut border and will taper off Sunday afternoon and evening. Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced to near-zero at times. Property damage is possible. Property or tree damage is possible. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to MBstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using MBStorm.

| Moderate - possible threat | Expected - act within an hour

item.title: Corn, Soybean & Oilseed Performance Workshop - Winsloe
item.description:
Corn, Soybean & Oilseed Performance Workshop - Winsloe slmacneil Thu, 10/22/2026 - 08:53

The 2027 PEI Field Crop Performance Series will bring together trends from ACE Network field data, firsthand experiences from producers and agronomists, and insight from crop specialists. Presentations and discussions will explore what is working in the field today, as well as emerging trends and practices that could help Atlantic Canadian producers advance crop yield and quality in the future.

Come compare experiences, ask questions and take home practical ideas to consider for your farm.

Join us for the 2027 PEI Field Crop Performance Series, featuring practical ideas, farmer experiences and conversations about what is working in the field.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”
